newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila T-bill mkt inactive, banks remain cautious.
newsitem.headline: Manila T-bill mkt inactive, banks remain cautious.

text.p: Manila's secondary market for Treasury bills saw few trades on Tuesday as banks remained wary over the outlook for interest rates, traders said.
Traders said there was no appetite for T-bills even after rates moved up at Monday's auction because the Central Bank's overnight borrowing rate remained at 15 percent.
"There's a negative carry," a trader said, saying the short-term T-bills were lower than the Central Bank's key rate of 15 percent.
"There would have been demand at these levels if the overnight rate had fallen," the same trader said.
Late last week, the Central Bank was forced to raise rates to protect the peso from speculation brought on by the problems of the Thai baht.
At the interbank call loan market, the average rate was anchored at 15.0625 percent as the Central Bank kept a floor on rates throught its overnight borrowing.
Volume nudged down to 20.41 billion pesos from 20.92 billion pesos. Among the 53 participating financial institutions, 32 were lenders.
